ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The transition-state drawing shows a Cl3Al fragment on the left, with Al connected toward a central chlorine atom. The central chlorine is connected to a carbonyl carbon. The carbonyl carbon is double-bonded to oxygen and single-bonded to hydrogen. Curved arrows and charge symbols are also shown, but the question says to disregard arrows and exclude bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning: Following the assigned method, expand the Cl3Al component as three Al–Cl bonds. Then count the other non-hydrogen bonds explicitly present in the transition-state drawing: one additional Al–Cl bond from Al to the central chlorine, one C–Cl bond, and one C=O bond. The C–H bond is excluded because it involves hydrogen. Therefore the total is 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6.
